Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Chris Verrone and Todd Sohn interpret the rebound as a return to AI, power and bank leadership, with faster risk-taking than in 2025. They discuss gold's changing behavior, software capitulation, credit versus geopolitical risk and passive semiconductor concentration. Verrone expects a possible melt-up; Eisman reports that view and emphasizes benign bank credit. Their technical indicators are hypotheses requiring defined, independent price tests. Energy's prewar uptrend explicitly challenges an exclusively war-driven account.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Use price behavior to challenge intuitive macro narratives.
- Oversold is a condition, not an automatic purchase signal.
- Inspect look-through sector concentration in passive funds.
- Separate financial contagion from geopolitical headlines.
- Retain false signals and changing market structure when using historical analogies.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- ETF net inflows versus trading volume.
- Gold correlations and precious-metal ETF turnover.
- Semiconductor and software index weights.
- Software trend lines and relative performance.
- Bank charts and credit spreads.
- Sector relative strength and ETF launches.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman hosts; Chris Verrone provides most market-regime and trend interpretations; Todd Sohn provides ETF, flow and concentration observations. Joint guest attribution is used for short ambiguous exchanges. Closing melt-up statement credits Chris explicitly.
- Full transcript read in two contiguous parts, including long advertisement break.
- Recording date explicitly April 27, earlier than May 4 publication.
- Chris Verrone is sometimes transcribed as Ferrone; Todd Sohn has distinct flow/ETF comments.
- Where rapid guest exchanges make exact attribution uncertain, joint attribution is used and excluded from Eisman scoring.
